<!-- This is an auto-generated comment by CodeRabbit for review status -->

The substance here is good, and better than the `test:` title suggests — threading `api.Clock` into `ParseTimeParameter` is a real fix, and you updated all four production call sites and all five test call sites consistently. The omitted-`time` test is genuinely load-bearing too: it fails without the clock change, because the fixture trip only falls inside the window at the pinned clock. That's the right way to write a regression test.

One blocker, and it isn't about your code.

**This won't compile once merged.** It calls `createTestApiWithTripsForRouteFixture`, which was removed from `main` and replaced by the generic `createTestApiWithGTFSFixture(t, clock, zipName, files)`. Merging your branch into current `main` locally and running `go vet`:

```
internal/restapi/trips_for_route_handler_test.go:422:9: undefined: createTestApiWithTripsForRouteFixture
```

The PR shows MERGEABLE with every check green because CI ran against a merge ref computed before that helper was deleted — so nothing on our side flagged it. Rebasing onto current `main` and porting the two new tests to `createTestApiWithGTFSFixture` should be all it takes.

While you're in there, one small thing this PR invalidates: the comment at `trips_for_route_handler_test.go:152` still says "ParseTimeParameter ignores api.Clock when no time= is given", which your own fix makes untrue. It's on a line you didn't touch, but this is the change that breaks it.

Worth splitting the title/description too — a signature change to a shared util under a `test:` heading is easy to miss in the log. Your commits do delineate the two concerns properly, which is the part that actually matters.

Re-review as soon as it's rebased; the fix itself I'm happy with.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment by CodeRabbit for review status -->

This looks good — ready to merge.

The clock threading is complete and consistent. I grepped for `ParseTimeParameter` and all four production call sites are updated with no stragglers, and since `createClock` returns `clock.RealClock{}` for everything but the test environment, this is a genuine no-op in production — the only reachable behavior change is under a mock clock, which is the whole point.

What I appreciated is that the new tests actually depend on the change. `TestTripsForRouteHandler_TimeOmitted` only passes because the fixture trip falls inside the window of the pinned clock; under the old `time.Now()` behavior it would fail outside a narrow wall-clock window. That is the difference between a test that documents behavior and one that just happens to be green.

The stale comment I flagged last time ("ParseTimeParameter ignores api.Clock when no time= is given") is gone and replaced with an accurate one.
